chunks: From him, from his father, from Fazalat, from Dawood ibn Farqad, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Angels used to reckon that Iblees was from them, and it was in the Knowledge of Allah that he was not from them. So he brought out what was within himself with prejudice and anger, so he said: 'You created me from fire and You created him from clay'.

key_terms.إِبْلِيسَ: Iblees (Satan), the jinn who disobeyed Allah.
key_terms.الْحَمِيَّةُ: Prejudice, zeal, or tribal pride; a sense of superiority based on origin or status.
key_terms.الْغَضَبُ: Anger or wrath; the emotional response that drove Iblees to speak out.
key_terms.الْمَلَائِكَةَ: The Angels, who assumed Iblees was among them.
key_terms.طِينٍ: Clay, the material from which Adam was created.

ai.seo_question: What caused Iblees's arrogance and fall according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this hadith from *Al-Kafi* identifies 'al-hamiyyah' (tribal or innate prejudice) as the root of Iblees's fall, illustrating how a single flaw in character can lead to disobedience despite high status. The narrative underscores that the Angels' assumption of his inclusion was based on outward proximity, whereas Allah's knowledge revealed his inner distinctness, a theme central to understanding human potential for both elevation and degradation. This incident serves as a foundational lesson in *adab* (etiquette) and self-awareness within Shia moral theology.
